statements.status_notes: GHSA-4xr6-hc3h-f6jq (GO-2026-6940): ws.ReadFrame, ws.MustReadFrame and the wsutil message readers in github.com/gobwas/ws allocate a buffer of the payload length a frame header declares before any payload arrives, so a peer can declare a huge frame and exhaust memory. github.com/gobwas/ws 1.5.0 fixes it with https://github.com/gobwas/ws/commit/6b485812604c20a7174f3d68a64379121bcddfe2: https://github.com/gobwas/ws/security/advisories/GHSA-4xr6-hc3h-f6jq, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6940. We read the Go build information of /usr/bin/grafana-image-renderer, the only file in the package, in every published grafana-image-renderer-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 2026-11-27: 26 builds from 5.10.1-r0 to the current 5.12.11-r2, for both x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against its index checksum. The program is a statically linked Go executable (no ELF interpreter and no shared-library dependencies) built with CGO_ENABLED=0, without -trimpath and without the -s and -w linker flags, so it keeps its ELF symbol table. Their build information lists github.com/gobwas/ws 1.4.0 in 5.10.1-r0 to 5.12.11-r1 and 1.5.0 in 5.12.11-r2, the same on both architectures and in the base and -dev packages. We also downloaded five Alpine 3.23 packages, checked each against its index size and the program's MD5 in the full scan, and searched their programs byte by byte: grafana-image-renderer 5.10.1-r0 and 5.12.10-r1 for x86_64, 5.12.6-r0 and 5.12.11-r2 for aarch64, and grafana-image-renderer-dev 5.12.1-r1 for x86_64. The Alpine 3.24 and Debian packages of the same version and architecture carry the same program. The WebSocket reader is linked: the five programs above contain github.com/gobwas/ws/wsutil.(*Reader) methods (NextFrame, Read and readHeader in the -dev program's symbol table). We set the fixed boundary at 5.12.11-r2, the first build with github.com/gobwas/ws 1.5.0.

GHSA-4xr6-hc3h-f6jq (GO-2026-6940): ws.ReadFrame, ws.MustReadFrame and the wsutil message readers in github.com/gobwas/ws allocate a buffer of the payload length a frame header declares before any payload arrives, so a peer can declare a huge frame and exhaust memory. github.com/gobwas/ws 1.5.0 fixes it with https://github.com/gobwas/ws/commit/6b485812604c20a7174f3d68a64379121bcddfe2: https://github.com/gobwas/ws/security/advisories/GHSA-4xr6-hc3h-f6jq, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6940. The grafana-image-renderer-fips-dev packages for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository, which requires authentication, are built separately from the non-FIPS grafana-image-renderer packages, and we have not yet read the Go build information of every published grafana-image-renderer-fips-dev build. Pending: that per-build read on both architectures, to establish which github.com/gobwas/ws version each FIPS build ships and so where its fixed boundary falls. For comparison, the only non-FIPS grafana-image-renderer build with github.com/gobwas/ws 1.5.0 is 5.12.11-r2. That does not establish the same of the FIPS builds.
